To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
floating gate cells are vulnerable to low-energy proton direct ionization, and that the error rate is strongly affected by the thickness and composition of the overlayers.

single event upsets can be induced by direct ionization from protons in floating gate cells, that the energy loss in the silicon oxide overlayers is the main source of the proton threshold, and that the error rate is proportional to the square of the proton energy in the energy range from a few tens of MeV up to 200 MeV.

(1) proton single event upsets in floating gate cells are observed; (2) the threshold LET is 0.2–0.3 MeV/(mg/cm2); (3) the error rate is proportional to the particle track size and to the square of the overlayer thickness; (4) the threshold LET decreases with technology scaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the physical mechanisms that cause Single Event Effects (SEEs), and the study of their effects in electronic devices.
the study of the physical mechanisms responsible for the single event upsets in floating gate cells.
the study of the effects of single events in floating gate cells, induced by low-energy protons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single-event-upsets in floating-gate cells are induced by direct ionization, and that the threshold LET is determined by the track size, and not by the ion energy.
proton induced single event upset (SEU) is a real threat for floating gate memories.
the floating gate cell is not a robust memory cell against single event upsets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proton direct ionization is a significant error mechanism for floating gate cells in advanced Flash memories.
the proton direct ionization is a serious threat to the reliability of floating gate memories, especially for the multi-level cell devices, where the error threshold is much lower.
the single-event upset rate due to low-energy protons is a critical issue for the next generation of Flash memories.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the floating gate error rates induced by low energy protons are comparable with those induced by heavy ions, and the threshold LET for floating gates is expected to scale with technology down to the 3D NAND generation.
the floating gate error rate is not a monotonic function of the LET.
the error rate induced by proton direct ionizations is expected to increase by more than two orders of magnitude for each technology node.
